My farm is only 3.8 mu so I have to plan carefully. Chili is what pays — in our village almost everyone grows it and the dealers come right to the road to buy dried chili in autumn. I will put 3 mu in chili and keep 0.8 mu in spring maize for the family and for pig feed. My husband works in the city part of the year so I handle most of the field work with help from my mother-in-law.

For chili, I buy transplants from the seedling shed near the county town — hybrid variety, the long red kind that dries well. Last year my neighbor got over 350 jin of dry chili per mu with that seed so I will use the same. Chili is a hungry crop. I spread about 3 cart-loads of chicken manure per mu before transplanting, then for the base fertilizer I use about 2 bags of compound fertilizer 15-15-15 per mu (that's 100 jin, roughly 25 kg N, 25 kg P, 25 kg K split across the NPK when I add topdressing). During the season I topdress twice with urea, about 30 jin per mu each time, and add potassium sulfate when fruits start setting because the dealer told me low potassium makes the chili skin thin. Well irrigation I use 7 or 8 times — chili cannot stand dry soil when flowering. Pesticide I cannot skip — aphids, thrips, and anthracnose all come. I spray about 8 times through the season, sometimes mixing two medicines to save labor. Rotary tillage before transplanting, plastic mulch on the ridges to save water and keep weeds down.

For maize, I use Zhengdan or Xianyu hybrid seed like my neighbors. I apply 1 bag of compound 15-15-15 at sowing and topdress urea at big trumpet stage, maybe 25 jin. Two irrigations if the rain is short, one spray for armyworm and corn borer. I expect around 550 kg per mu — not bad for spring maize here.
